title: Pipeline measurement — plan 001
epic_title: Build the pipeline-measurement tool — per-phase spend & efficiency across the four harnesses

tasks.title: The per-run record store and schema
tasks.goal: A schema-versioned JSON run record can be appended to and read back from an append-only JSONL store, one file per run.
tasks.desired: A record type carrying a schema version, run id, feature id, phase id, harness, per-model spend slots, efficiency slots, price-snapshot version, and unavailable markers, serialized one-per-line to a per-run file in a gitignored observability-logs location; a loader reads a run's records back; two concurrent runs write distinct files and never contend; unknown/missing optional fields default on read (additive-schema).
scope: The record type and its schema version.
The per-run-file append and the run loader.
The gitignore entry for the store location.
out_of_scope: Capturing spend or efficiency, or deriving cost (later tasks).
acceptance: Writing N records to a run then loading that run yields exactly N equal records.
Two runs writing concurrently produce two distinct files with no lost or interleaved lines.
A record missing an optional field loads with that field defaulted, never an error.
key_interfaces: The run-record struct (schema-versioned); the store's append-one and load-run contracts.

tasks.title: Phase-boundary detection and innermost-active-phase attribution
tasks.goal: The recorder brackets a run's phases from the harness's own session record as a stack and attributes each turn to the innermost active phase.
tasks.current: No phase concept exists over a harness session record.
tasks.desired: A phase stack where a skill-invocation marker pushes and an artifact-write pops; each turn attributes to the top of the stack; a nested sub-skill gets its own bracket and record, never blended into its parent; a phase with no close is recorded incomplete with its spend, never dropped or rolled into the next; each phase carries the identity of the harness that ran it.
scope: The phase-stack detector over a harness session record; the push/pop marker predicates.
Incomplete-phase handling and per-phase harness identity.
out_of_scope: Reading spend figures or writing the spend fields (T3).
acceptance: A nested-invocation fixture yields distinct phase brackets with no spend blended into the parent.
An aborted phase (no close marker) is recorded incomplete, never dropped or merged into the next.
A harness-switch fixture yields records each naming the harness that ran that phase.
key_interfaces: The phase-stack type; the boundary-marker predicates (open/close).

tasks.title: Spend-source port + Claude Code adapter: measure a phase end to end
tasks.goal: Measure a real Claude Code phase's per-model spend and write its record — the first end-to-end measured phase.
tasks.desired: A consumer-side spend-source port; a Claude Code adapter that reads Claude Code's own accounting for a phase bracket into a per-model token quartet; the recorder writes the phase's record (spend + harness + ids) to the store. The recorder invokes no model, reads only accounting + the run, mutates nothing of the run, writes no secret value, and its main refuses a flag-like positional before any write.
scope: The Claude Code adapter; the record-write path; the recorder main (fail-closed on misparse).
out_of_scope: The other three adapters (T6–T8); reconciliation (T4); the degradation path (T5).
acceptance: Running a real Claude Code phase yields a record whose per-model tokens equal Claude Code's own accounting for that bracket.
Over a full measurement pass the recorder consumes zero model tokens and leaves the run's artifacts and harness state byte-unchanged.
A seeded-secret transcript produces no record containing the secret.
A flag-like positional (e.g. a flag placed after a directory arg) is refused as a usage error before any record is written.
key_interfaces: The spend-source port; the Claude Code adapter (implements it); the recorder entrypoint.
tasks.size_accepted: the first end-to-end tracer bullet — the port, the primary adapter, the record-write path, and the recorder main are one demoable slice; splitting them yields no independently-demoable behavior

tasks.title: Tiered reconciliation
tasks.goal: Each recorded per-model figure is reconciled to the harness's own accounting, with the reconciliation tier recorded per figure.
tasks.desired: The recorder cross-checks the per-phase per-model sum against the harness's authoritative total for the same span where one is reported, and records the tier — exact where the harness reports an authoritative figure, harness-precision where only a coarser figure exists (never inventing digits), unavailable where non-reconcilable.
scope: The reconciler and the per-figure tier recording.
acceptance: On a reference run every recorded figure carries a reconciliation tier.
An authoritative-total fixture reconciles exact (recorded equals the harness figure).
A coarser-total fixture records harness-precision and never reports more precision than the harness gave.
key_interfaces: The reconciler contract; the tier enum (exact / harness-precision / unavailable).

tasks.title: Honest degradation: unavailable, never a silent zero
tasks.goal: A figure a harness cannot expose is recorded as a declared unavailable marker, never a zero or an estimate.
tasks.current: An adapter that cannot read a figure has no defined recorded outcome.
tasks.desired: The spend-source port's contract lets an adapter return a declared unavailable marker naming the harness and the missing figure; the recorder writes the marker; no zero or estimated value is ever presented as measured spend.
scope: The unavailable marker type and the port's degradation contract; the recorder's handling of it.
out_of_scope: Which specific harnesses degrade (each adapter's empirical concern, T6–T8).
acceptance: A no-usage fixture yields a declared unavailable marker naming the harness and figure.
No zero or estimate ever appears where a figure was unavailable (a red-first-then-green degradation test).
key_interfaces: The unavailable marker type; the spend-source port's return contract.

tasks.title: Codex spend adapter
tasks.desired: A Codex adapter reading Codex's own accounting through whichever channel it exposes on the user's own key (the empirical capability-matrix spike), producing per-model spend for a phase bracket, or a declared unavailable where Codex exposes none. It alters no Codex state.
scope: The Codex adapter and the channel investigation for Codex.
out_of_scope: The port itself (T3); the other adapters.
acceptance: A Codex reference-run fixture yields per-model spend or a declared unavailable, attributed to the correct phase.
Reading Codex's accounting leaves Codex's own output byte-unchanged.
key_interfaces: The Codex adapter (implements the spend-source port).

tasks.title: Cursor CLI spend adapter
tasks.goal: Capture-or-declare per-model spend on Cursor CLI.
tasks.desired: A Cursor CLI adapter reading its accounting through whichever channel it exposes on the user's own key; the design flags Cursor's proxy-billing as the likeliest degradation case, so a declared unavailable is an expected, first-class outcome here, not a failure. It alters no Cursor state.
scope: The Cursor CLI adapter and the channel investigation for Cursor.
out_of_scope: The port itself (T3); the other adapters.
acceptance: A Cursor CLI reference-run fixture yields per-model spend or a declared unavailable, attributed to the correct phase.
Where Cursor exposes no per-model spend on the user's key, the adapter declares unavailable, never a fabricated figure.
key_interfaces: The Cursor CLI adapter (implements the spend-source port).

tasks.title: OpenCode spend adapter
tasks.desired: An OpenCode adapter reading its accounting through whichever channel it exposes on the user's own key, producing per-model spend for a phase bracket, or a declared unavailable. It alters no OpenCode state.
scope: The OpenCode adapter and the channel investigation for OpenCode.
out_of_scope: The port itself (T3); the other adapters.
acceptance: An OpenCode reference-run fixture yields per-model spend or a declared unavailable, attributed to the correct phase.
Reading OpenCode's accounting leaves OpenCode's own output byte-unchanged.
key_interfaces: The OpenCode adapter (implements the spend-source port).

tasks.title: Deterministic artifact+git efficiency reader
tasks.goal: Per-phase efficiency signals are computed deterministically from the frozen artifacts + git, joined to the run records.
tasks.desired: A reader counts the corpus's existing typed anchors per phase — questions from `D-n`, fog from `G-n`, rework from superseded `D-n` and amendment count, defects from review `FND-n`, coverage from the plan matrix, latency from git timestamps — joined to records by run/phase id, with no model invocation and no runtime hook, yielding identical signals whichever harness produced the artifacts.
scope: The anchor-counting extractor, the git-timestamp latency, and the join to records.
out_of_scope: Any spend path; the operator presentation (T12).
acceptance: For a reference run the efficiency signals are byte-identical when computed from two different harnesses' artifacts.
Computing the signals consumes zero model tokens.
key_interfaces: The efficiency-signal struct; the per-anchor-family counters; the git latency reader.

tasks.title: Vendor the pinned per-model price data
tasks.goal: The pinned upstream per-model price map is vendored as committed data, with a re-vendor script and a recorded version pin.
acceptance: The vendored price map is present as committed data at the recorded pin, and the re-vendor script reproduces it.
provenance: Vendor the pinned upstream per-model price map (the LiteLLM `model_prices_and_context_window.json`) as committed data in the footprint's vendor area.
Add a re-vendor script mirroring the pinned Mermaid-data vendoring idiom.
Record the pinned version in the footprint's version-pin file.
touches: the vendored price-data asset; the footprint version-pin file

tasks.title: Cost derivation from the vendored prices
tasks.goal: Each record's per-model dollar cost is derived from the pinned price snapshot, with the snapshot version stamped and un-priced models flagged.
tasks.current: Records carry tokens but no cost.
tasks.desired: Parse the vendored price data; compute per-model cost as tokens times the pinned per-class price; stamp the price-snapshot version on the record; flag an un-priced model rather than emitting a silent zero cost.
scope: The price parser and the cost derivation; the snapshot-version stamp; the un-priced flag.
out_of_scope: Maintaining the prices themselves (vendored, T10); the presentation (T12).
acceptance: A record reproduces its dollar cost from the price-snapshot version it stamped.
A model with no price entry is flagged, never given a $0 cost.
key_interfaces: The price-table parser; the cost-derivation contract; the snapshot-version field.

tasks.title: The operator reader
tasks.goal: The operator can read, per phase of a run, tokens by model, dollar cost, and the efficiency signals.
tasks.current: Records exist in the store but there is no operator-facing read.
tasks.desired: A reader that queries a run's records, joins the reconciled spend, cost, and efficiency, and presents each phase's tokens-by-model, cost, and efficiency signals (or the unavailable markers); its main fails closed on misparse.
scope: The reader main and the per-phase presentation.
out_of_scope: A query/analytics surface or a cost-per-feature rollup view (waiting room).
acceptance: For a reference run, the read lists every phase with its per-model tokens, cost, and efficiency signals, or the declared unavailable markers.
A flag-like positional is refused as a usage error before any read side effect.
key_interfaces: The reader entrypoint; the per-phase view contract.
